export_rights.summary: Salesforce's Main Services Agreement provides that, upon request made within 30 days after termination or expiration, Salesforce will make Your Data available for export or download; after that 30-day period Salesforce has no obligation to retain it and will delete or destroy copies unless legally prohibited.

covers: all standard and custom object records
routes.how: Setup -> Data Export (Data Export Service): Export Now or Schedule Export; org data is written to CSV files packaged into ZIP archives (~512 MB each) and a download link is emailed to the admin
requires: System Administrator or equivalent Setup access with data-export permission
Weekly exports: Enterprise/Performance/Unlimited Edition; monthly cadence on Professional Edition
routes.rate_limits: Weekly export available every 7 days on Enterprise/Performance/Unlimited; roughly every 29 days on Professional
gotchas: Export files are only available for download for 48 hours, and are deleted when a new export is generated
Attachments/documents/files are only included if the 'Include images, documents, and attachments' and 'Include Salesforce Files and Salesforce CRM Content document versions' checkboxes are selected
Including binary content substantially increases export size and processing time
Large exports are split across multiple ZIP files that must each be downloaded within the window

covers: any queryable standard or custom object (accounts, contacts, leads, opportunities, cases, activities, custom objects)
routes.how: Bulk API 2.0 query jobs: POST a SOQL query to /services/data/vXX.X/jobs/query with an OAuth 2.0 bearer token, poll job status, then download result sets; designed for result sets of 2,000+ records
requires: OAuth 2.0 access token (connected app) or session ID
routes.rate_limits: Bulk queries are documented as retrieving up to 15 GB of data per query, split into 1-GB result files; Bulk API jobs also draw on org-wide daily allocations documented in the Salesforce limits quick reference
gotchas: Binary fields (e.g. file bodies) are not returned in bulk query results; files require separate download (see file-storage route)
SOQL per-object queries mean you must enumerate objects yourself to get a whole-org copy

routes.how: REST API (/services/data/vXX.X/query?q=SOQL) and SOAP API with OAuth 2.0; Data Loader (Salesforce's free client) wraps these APIs to export any object to CSV via its Export wizard
requires: OAuth 2.0 connected app or Data Loader login
routes.rate_limits: Org-wide daily API request allocation applies to SOAP and REST calls; the allocation varies by edition and license count per Salesforce's 'API Request Limits and Allocations' quick reference (specific numbers not captured from the consulted excerpt)
gotchas: Daily API request allocation is shared org-wide with integrations; large extractions should prefer Bulk API 2.0

covers: any report over standard/custom objects (report-shaped record extracts)
routes.how: Reports tab -> open report -> Export; choose Formatted Report (xlsx) or Details Only (xlsx, xls, csv)
gotchas: XLSX exports (formatted or details-only) are capped at 100,000 rows and 100 columns
Details Only export to CSV/XLS bypasses the 2,000-row on-screen display limit

routes.how: Two documented paths: (1) include files in the Data Export Service via its attachment/Files checkboxes; (2) query ContentVersion (Id, ContentDocumentId, Title, VersionData) with Data Loader/SOQL, then download each binary via the REST API VersionData endpoint per Salesforce KB 000381137
requires: Data Loader or API access with rights to ContentVersion/Attachment records
gotchas: Data Loader exports of ContentVersion return metadata rows, not usable binaries in one step; the VersionData binary must be fetched per record via the REST API
Per-record binary download makes very large file libraries slow to extract; scripting over ContentVersion IDs is the documented pattern

covers: event-log-files (user activity: logins, API calls, report exports)
routes.how: Setup -> Quick Find -> 'View Setup Audit Trail' -> Download for the past 180 days of setup changes (CSV); user-activity logs via Event Monitoring's EventLogFile object, queried and downloaded through the API
requires: View Setup and Configuration (Setup access) for Setup Audit Trail
Event Monitoring add-on for full EventLogFile access; free tier limited to certain log types with 1-day retention
gotchas: Setup Audit Trail download covers only the trailing 180 days
Event Monitoring retains 30 days of event log files (up to 1 year for some log types at extra cost); the free subset retains only 1 day
Setup Audit Trail UI shows only the 20 most recent changes; the CSV download is required for full history

covers: page layouts, profiles, permission sets, Apex, flows and other Metadata API component types
routes.how: Metadata API retrieve() call (or 'sf project retrieve start' with a package.xml manifest) returns a ZIP of XML component files; the same ZIP is redeployable via deploy(), making it a restorable configuration artifact
requires: Modify Metadata / API access (typically System Administrator)
Salesforce CLI, Workbench, or another Metadata API client
gotchas: Not every configuration component type is supported by the Metadata API; check coverage for the org's customizations
A package.xml manifest must enumerate the component types to retrieve

preservation_notes.attachments: Bulk path exists: Data Export Service includes attachments/images/documents and Salesforce Files/CRM Content versions when the corresponding checkboxes are selected; outside that, Salesforce KB 000381137 documents querying ContentVersion and downloading each VersionData binary via the REST API (Data Loader alone yields metadata rows, not binaries).
preservation_notes.audit_log: Setup Audit Trail is downloadable as CSV from Setup covering the past 180 days. User-activity event log files (EventLogFile) require Event Monitoring; documented retention is 30 days (some log types up to 1 year at extra cost), and the free tier retains only 1 day. Field-history retention was not researched from the docs consulted.
preservation_notes.config_artifacts: Metadata API retrieve() returns a ZIP of XML component files driven by a package.xml manifest; the ZIP is a restorable artifact redeployable via deploy(). Report and dashboard definitions are among retrievable metadata types, subject to Metadata API coverage.

notes: Research caveats: help.salesforce.com, developer.salesforce.com, and www.salesforce.com were blocked by this environment's egress proxy for direct page fetches, so all claims were derived from vendor-doc content surfaced through web-search excerpts of the cited pages rather than full page fetches; verify each route in-tenant before relying on it. Unknowns left out on purpose: concrete daily API request allocation numbers per edition were not captured; field-history/Field Audit Trail retention was not researched; the exact name of the profile permission gating Setup -> Data Export was not confirmed; Data Export FAQ (help article 000383962) exists but its full text did not load. The 30-day post-termination export window was quoted from the Developer Services MSA PDF; the mainline Sales Cloud MSA is expected to carry the same clause but was not directly retrieved.
